text: But it’s my belief you’d sell yourself, if it was only for the pleasure of making somebody feel he’d got a bad bargain.” “Aye, aye,” said Dunstan, very placably, “you do me justice, I see. You know I’m a jewel for ’ticing people into bargains. For which reason I advise you to let me sell Wildfire. I’d ride him to the hunt to-morrow for you, with pleasure. I shouldn’t look so handsome as you in the saddle, but it’s the horse they’ll bid for, and not the rider.” “Yes, I daresay—trust my horse to you!” “As you please,” said Dunstan, rapping the window-seat again with an air of great unconcern.
